explanation: HTTP is just text sent over a socket, and the format is strict: every line ends with a carriage return plus a line feed (\r\n), and one empty line marks the end of the headers. A StringBuilder assembles the request cheaply, and copying the headers into a TreeMap sorts them by key for free because TreeMap keeps its keys in natural order. Getting these bytes exactly right is what makes a hand-written client work at all.
hints: Append the pieces to a StringBuilder in order: request line, Host line, header lines, then one more \r\n to close the headers.
new TreeMap<>(headers) gives you the same entries sorted by key, so a plain for-each over entrySet() emits them in order.
Write \r\n at the end of EVERY line, including the last header, and remember the extra blank line at the very end.
